Please read before continuing.


The information provided in this map is compiled from various sources, including Georgetown County, municipal governments, state and federal agencies. Georgetown County does not guarantee the accuracy, completeness, or currency of the data provided. In no event shall Georgetown County be liable for any special, indirect, incidental, or consequential damages arising from the use of, or reliance on, the information contained herein.


This website is intended to serve as a secondary representation of real property and other geographic information within the County and is compiled from recorded deeds, plats, public records, and other available sources, which remain the primary sources for such information. Users are advised to consult the appropriate primary source documents and agencies for verification of the information presented here.


The map layers and data displayed do not replace a legal survey, deed, plat, or other official documentation. The GIS maps and data provided herein are intended for informational, governmental, research, and internal business use purposes and shall not be redistributed or represented as official authoritative records without permission from Georgetown County.

GETTING STARTED

Use this interactive map to explore Georgetown County data, including parcels, zoning, roads, flood zones, and more. You can search for an address, turn layers on/off, and click features to view detailed information.


 

Search Bar

Use the Search Bar to find a location by TMS Number, address, or road name.

TMS Number: A unique number used to identify a property parcel that contains 13 digits. For example: 05-0029-049-00-00. Please follow this format, including the hyphens (-), when entering a TMS Number in the search bar.

Address or Road Name: Spell out road directions, but abbreviate the road type. Examples:

SOUTH HAZARD ST — not S HAZARD ST

HAGLEY DR — not HAGLEY DRIVE


 

Layer List

Turn map layers on/off

Expand groups (e.g., Parcels, Zoning, Boundaries)

Click a layer to explore available data


 

Legend

Explains map symbols and colors

Updates automatically based on visible layers 


 

Swipe Tool

The Swipe tool allows users analyze layers against other layers to ascertain change. For example the difference between 2023 aerial photos vs 2024. 


 

Basemaps

Basemaps can be easily changed, the default is OpenStreetMap. Basemaps are a courtesy and not maintained by the County. As such, often they may contain contradictory information. For example, street names can vary between these basemaps and are sometimes incorrect. 


 

Add Data

Users can search ArcGIS Online or upload their own data within the map. These added data are only available while you have the web browser open.


 

Share

Use the Share button to create a link to your current map view. Be sure to check “Include URL parameters” so others see the same location and layers as you.


Additional Resources


  1. Georgetown Deeds - This is the Register of Deeds research portal and can be used to enter owner, plat references, deed book or page, or information from the legal description that may be relevant to researching documents online. Please note plat slides need an S added in front of them, e.g. S839-2  
  2. Zoning Setbacks -This table can be used to research property setbacks based upon its zoning designation.
  3. ﻿Land Use/Zoning Designation Chart - This table can be used to match zoning districts with Comprehensive Plan Future Land Use categories and also includes lot area minimums and setbacks.  
  4. qPublic - This is the County Assessors database which has full property information and is searchable in numerous ways.
